text: `ns.stream().peek(seen::add).filter(n -> n > 3).findFirst()` over the list 1 to 10 reported examining `[1, 2, 3, 4]`. Why only four?
choices: `peek` samples the stream rather than observing every element that passes.
The stream was split into batches of four, and only the first batch was needed.
`filter` evaluated its predicate on the first four elements and cached the rest.
Streams are lazy — elements are pulled through the whole pipeline one at a time, and `findFirst` stopped as soon as it had an answer.
explanation: The hand-written `filter` from Section 26.2.1 cannot do this: it builds the entire filtered list, then `findFirst` looks at element zero, having done ten times the necessary work. On a million-element list where the answer is early, that is the difference between instant and slow. The same mechanism is what makes `Stream.iterate(1, n -> n * 2).limit(10)` terminate over an infinite source.
